meta.title: The One-Day Protocol
meta.subtitle: An interactive model of "How to fix your entire life in 1 day"
meta.sourceWork: How to fix your entire life in 1 day
meta.disclaimer: Educational and self-reflection material. Not therapy, medical, or mental-health advice.

root.label: How to fix your entire life in 1 day
root.note: A model of the ideas in Dan Koe's "How to fix your entire life in 1 day", organised after the mind map by @MindBranches.

children.label: Core Problem
Change fails at the action layer
children.note: People swap behaviours while leaving their identity untouched, so the old self quietly reinstalls the old behaviour.

children.label: You need the person, not the plan
children.note: The durable move is becoming someone for whom the desired actions are simply the obvious ones.

children.label: Your current life is not an accident
children.note: Today's behaviour is already succeeding at goals you never consciously chose. That is exactly why it survives.

children.label: Key Psychological Principles
Identity First, Actions Second
Effort is a symptom, not a strategy
children.note: People who look like they are grinding are usually just living a life that fits them.

children.label: Adopt the lifestyle before the outcome
children.note: Live as the person who already has the result. The result is what that life produces.

children.label: Misfit habits should start to repel you
children.note: Once identity actually shifts, old habits stop feeling tempting and start feeling wrong.

children.label: Understanding Your Mind
Behaviour is goal-directed
children.note: Nothing you do is random. Every pattern is aimed at something (teleology).

children.label: Some of those goals work against you
children.note: You can pursue a goal for years without ever having chosen it.

children.label: Change the goal, not just the schedule
children.note: New perspective produces new goals, which produce new behaviour. In that order.

children.label: Identity defends itself
children.note: Your sense of self reacts to contradiction the way your body reacts to infection.

children.label: The Anatomy of Identity
The identity loop
children.note: Set a goal, perceive reality through it, notice what is relevant, act and get feedback, repeat until automatic, it becomes "who you are", you defend it, and it starts generating your next goals.

children.label: It started before you were consulted
children.note: Most of the loop was installed in childhood by environment and conditioning.

children.label: After survival comes ideology
children.note: Once the body is safe, you begin defending beliefs as if they were food and shelter.

children.label: Stages of Mind Development
Most people sit between self-aware and construct-aware
children.note: Roughly stages 4 to 8 in adult-development models.

children.label: Development is sequential
children.note: You cannot skip a stage. You can only move through the next one.

children.label: The upper stages question inherited beliefs
children.note: That is where you stop borrowing principles and start writing your own.

children.label: Intelligence Framework
Intelligence = getting what you actually want
children.note: A working definition, not an IQ score.

children.label: Three ingredients: agency, opportunity, intelligence
children.note: Remove any one of the three and results stall.

children.label: The cybernetic loop
children.note: Set a goal, act, sense where you are, compare to the goal, adjust. Then repeat.

children.label: High intelligence = iteration speed
children.note: Persisting and learning from mistakes beats being right early.

children.label: The One-Day Protocol
Part 1 — Morning: Psychological Excavation
children.note: 15–30 minutes of honest writing, before the day gets loud.

children.label: Anti-Vision Questions
What dissatisfaction have you quietly learned to tolerate?
What do you complain about repeatedly and never change?
What true thing about your life would be unbearable to say out loud?
Five years out, nothing changes. Describe an ordinary Tuesday.
Ten years out, same trajectory. Which doors have closed for good?
At the end of your life, what did you never once attempt?
Which identity would you have to stop defending in order to change?
What is the embarrassing, real reason you have not changed yet?
Vision Questions
Three years out, best realistic case. Describe an ordinary Tuesday in detail.
What would you have to believe about yourself for that life to feel normal?
If you were already that person, what would you do this week?
Part 2 — Throughout the Day: Pattern Interruption
children.note: Six alarms that catch you mid-behaviour, plus three questions to carry around.

children.label: Phone reminders
What am I avoiding right now?
Judging only by my behaviour today, what would a stranger say I want?
Is this moving me toward the life I want or the one I dread?
What important thing am I pretending is not important?
Today, what did I do to protect my image rather than to get what I want?
When did I feel most alive today? Most dead?
Carry-around questions
What changes if I stop needing people to see me as ______?
Where am I trading aliveness for safety?
What is the smallest version of my future self I could be tomorrow?
Part 3 — Evening: Synthesis
children.note: Turn the day's raw material into two sentences and three goals.

children.label: Integration questions
Why, specifically, have you been stuck?
Name the internal enemy: which pattern or belief is actually running this?
One sentence: what you refuse to let your life become.
One sentence: what you are building toward.
Goal setting — lenses, not finish lines
1 year: what would have to be true for you to know the pattern is broken?
1 month: what must be true this month to keep the 1-year goal possible?
Daily: which 2–3 actions would your future self simply do, without debate?
Implementation: Turn Life Into a Game
Six Components to Document
Anti-vision
children.note: The life you refuse to end up in.
children.mechanic: What is at stake if you lose.

children.label: Vision
children.note: The life you are building toward.

children.label: 1-year goal
children.note: What is true twelve months from now.

children.label: 1-month project
children.note: The skill to acquire or the thing to build.
children.mechanic: The boss fight, where the XP comes from.

children.label: Daily levers
children.note: The 2–3 tasks that actually move it.

children.label: Constraints
children.note: What you will not sacrifice to get it.

children.label: Game Mechanics
Vision = the win condition
Anti-vision = what is at stake if you lose
1-year goal = the main mission
1-month project = the boss fight
Daily levers = daily quests
Constraints = the rules that force creativity
Critical Insights
Change is sudden, but only after tension builds
children.note: Dissonance leads to uncertainty, uncertainty leads to discovery.

children.label: Clarity compresses time, hours do not
children.note: You cannot make six years of progress in six months without knowing exactly what you are aiming at.

children.label: This takes one full day of focused work
children.note: Half-doing it produces half-answers.

children.label: It lands differently depending on your chapter
children.note: Timing is part of the result. The same questions hit harder at some points in life than others.

children.label: Questioning is thinking
children.note: Most of what passes for thinking is rehearsing things you already believe.

children.label: Your goals build your reality
children.note: They decide what you notice and what you treat as valuable.
